Complete multilingual support in Field Desk for English, German, and Arabic.

Users should be able to use the whole application in any of these languages, with consistent translations and appropriate number, currency, and plural formatting. Arabic should use RTL; English and German should use LTR.

The selected language should persist for each operator when navigating, reloading, and returning to the application. Changing language should preserve application state and user data.

Follow the existing architecture, approved catalogs, and data contracts in `docs/architecture.md`. Keep existing routes and unrelated product behavior working.

Run `python /app/serve.py --port 8000 --data /tmp/field-desk-dev` and verify the application in the browser in all three languages. Deliver changes under `/app`.

Write `/app/output/completion.json` with `status` (`"complete"` or `"partial"`) and `known_issues` (a list of remaining issue descriptions). Use an empty list only when there are no known issues. In your final response, summarize what you changed, what you verified, and anything incomplete.

# Field Desk

Original fixture application created for this assignment. It is not copied or adapted from an existing application repository.

- `serve.py`: local HTTP API, static files and SQLite data. The `--data` directory isolates each instance.
- `static/app.js`: event delegation, view/modal state, actions and operator selection.
- `static/core/`: requests, state, text formatting, locale prototype and shared shell.
- `static/views/`: eight workflow modules.
- `static/locales/`: approved English/German/Arabic copy, including plural branches and parameter names.

The locale selector is a prototype; it is not a statement that the product already supports a complete locale rollout. Work-order titles, customer and crew names, part names, and charge memos are user/domain data. Machine-facing status/error codes and CSV fields are deliberately independent of the UI language.

The local operators have no login or external identity provider. This is the documented container/demo deployment, not a production authentication exercise. Robin starts with English and notifications enabled; Amal starts with German and notifications disabled.

## Locale behavior and existing contracts

All eight views (orders, dispatch, parts, billing, activity, reports, settings and help) participate in the rollout, including shared navigation, headings, table headers, field labels/placeholders/accessibility names, empty states, errors, confirmations, notifications and help feedback. Use the supplied catalog key/value pairs unchanged; new keys may be added. Field Desk branding, operator/crew/part/customer names, and user-entered titles and memos remain data.

Changing language updates open dialogs, active errors, selection counts and visible notifications immediately. Preserve the route, search/status filter, selected orders, draft text and the meaning of entered amounts. Keep the existing `data-testid` controls available. Set document language/direction and place navigation appropriately for RTL/LTR.

Store locale through the existing preferences API for the selected operator. Navigation, reload and operator switches restore that operator's locale; changing it preserves the saved notification preference.

Format euro amounts and quantities for the selected locale, including the supplied Arabic zero/one/two/few/many/other plural forms. Seed stock counts cover all six Arabic branches. Equivalent Arabic digit/separator presentation, whitespace and bidirectional marks are accepted.

Money inputs accept normal locale grouping/decimal syntax: English `1,234.50`, German `1.234,50` and Arabic `١٬٢٣٤٫٥٠` all mean 123450 cents. Accept Arabic-Indic quantity digits. Amounts are nonnegative, at most 99999999 cents, with at most two fractional digits. Reject malformed input instead of truncating it. Preserve an open amount draft's numeric meaning across language changes; send/store integer cents.

Keep routes, operator IDs and status codes (`OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, `DONE`) stable. API errors retain their codes, fields and English `message` values; translate their UI presentation. CSV exports retain filename `work-orders.csv`, columns `order_id,title,status,budget_minor,crew_id`, raw user text, original status codes and integer-cent values. Stored event payloads remain data and render in the current locale.

    print('errs',errs); b.close()

steps.message:
Field Desk now works fully in English, German and Arabic. Arabic is right-to-left, and each operator's language is saved to the server and comes back on navigation, reload and operator switching. I tested all eight views, the dialogs and the main flows in Chromium (Playwright) in every language, and found no errors. `/app/output/completion.json` is written with status `complete` and an empty `known_issues` list. I left the changes uncommitted.

**What changed (all in `/app/static`)**
- **Translation core (`core/locale.js`)**: text now comes from the selected language's catalog instead of always English, with an English fallback for missing keys. Plurals follow each language's rules, including the six Arabic forms, and numbers inside messages are formatted for the language. Arabic uses Arabic-Indic digits. In Arabic, inserted user data (titles, names) is wrapped in invisible direction marks so Latin text doesn't scramble the sentence. The page's `lang` and direction are set from the language.
- **Formatting (`core/format.js`)**:
  - Euro amounts and quantities are shown in the selected language's format.
  - Money input is parsed strictly per language and stored as integer cents: English `1,234.50`, German `1.234,50` and Arabic `١٬٢٣٤٫٥٠` all give 123450.
  - Malformed input (bad grouping, three decimals, negatives, over 99999999 cents) is rejected rather than truncated.
  - Quantities accept Arabic-Indic digits.
- **Views and shell**: every hard-coded English string is now a catalog key, covering navigation, headings, table headers, labels, placeholders, accessibility labels, empty states, dialogs, errors, notifications, activity events and the help "copy" text and result. I used the supplied catalog entries unchanged and didn't need to add any new keys. Translated text is HTML-escaped, which also fixes a spot where a crew name was inserted unescaped. User-entered fields detect their own text direction.
- **App logic (`app.js`)**:
  - Changing language saves it through the existing preferences API while keeping the operator's saved notification setting. It keeps the route, search, filter, selected orders, open dialogs, errors and notifications on screen.
  - An open amount draft is rewritten in the new language's format with the same value. A draft that can't be parsed is kept as typed and still read with its original meaning.
  - The old shared browser-stored language setting is gone.
  - An unsaved notifications checkbox now survives a language change.
  - One bug I found while testing is fixed: a late `change` event could put the old amount text back after it had been converted.
- **Styles (`style.css`)**: removed the forced left-to-right layout so the navigation moves to the right in Arabic. The close button, toast position and the arrow on the "Assign crew" button now flip for right-to-left.

**What I verified**
